A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RISE research despite the changed title. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original multilingual and cross-model transfer experiments, BLiMP/SICK evaluations, centroid analyses, and random-prototype comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds MDV/Procrustes comparisons and an English negation-classification experiment.

M1.justification: RISE's canonicalization, averaging of aligned logarithmic-map vectors, and exponential-map prediction remain unchanged in Equations 1–3 and Appendix A. The new illustration, comparators, and downstream evaluation do not modify the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: The three datasets, seven languages, and three transformation phenomena remain. Appendix G adds English negation classification on unpaired sentences, extending evaluation beyond predicting transformed embeddings without broadening language or domain coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Mean Difference Vectors (MDV) and Procrustes as evaluated comparators across the synthetic multilingual, BLiMP, and SICK experiments in Section 6.4 and Appendix C. MDV also participates in downstream classification. This substantially expands comparison beyond v1's random prototypes, which remain.

E3.justification: Appendix G introduces classification using method-transformed training examples and a held-out set of 1,919 unpaired sentences: 961 with negation and 958 without. Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 supplement cosine similarity. Existing generation settings and the stated 80/20 cross-model split remain unchanged; settings for the new baseline comparisons are incompletely specified.

E4.justification: The centroid-consistency analyses in Appendix B and random-prototype robustness comparisons in v1 Appendix F, relocated to v2 Appendix H, are retained. The added comparator evaluations and downstream classification supply benchmark/task results, without a separate new ablation, sensitivity, error, or distribution-shift analysis.

E5.justification: New Figure 11 reports standard-deviation error bars across BLiMP/SICK examples. The existing 10,000 random-prototype trials, standard errors, confidence intervals, and significance reporting remain unchanged. No increase in repeated training runs is documented.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands results through comparative transfer heatmaps and new benchmark and classification outcomes. Figure 11 places Procrustes highest on BLiMP (0.9894), while RISE leads SICK (0.8426 versus MDV 0.8328 and Procrustes 0.6738). Table 9 reports negation accuracy of 0.930 for RISE versus 0.872 for MDV. Original tables and plot content remain; the new scores do not establish same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the same sphere definitions, exponential/logarithmic maps, rotor constructions, first-order commutativity theorem and proof, and linear-complexity proposition. Removing its introductory roadmap does not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The central claim of transferable geometric structure supporting sentence-level LRH remains. v2 narrows the framing toward semantic-syntactic interpretation and emphasizes transformations with clear syntactic mappings, reducing semantic-control and universal-representation claims. Conversely, the abstract strengthens 'high transfer of performance' to 'without reducing performance.'

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit cosine-score interpretation bands and explains MDV/RISE performance versus Procrustes through spherical geometry and the rigidity of a global rotation. It also interprets the downstream classification results. Existing qualifications about syntactic versus semantic effectiveness, English-centric bias, limited coverage, and synthetic-data bias are largely retained or relocated.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a repository link in Section 1 and describes MDV's use of logarithmic/exponential maps. Existing prompt templates, generation hyperparameters, deduplication procedures, and RISE implementation details remain. The added experiments still lack detailed comparator and classifier specifications.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Mitchell and Lapata, Baroni and Zamparelli, Artetxe et al., and Conneau et al., while removing nostalgebraist and Feng et al. The main LRH and geometric-steering positioning remains. Several other reference changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: The title, affiliation, and publication header change, and semantic-syntactic terminology becomes consistent throughout. Discussion and limitations are consolidated, the standalone broader-implications section disappears, and the conclusion is revised. Most methodological exposition, theory, and existing appendix prose remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds a step-by-step method illustration, three comparative transfer-heatmap figures, a BLiMP/SICK bar chart, interpretation and baseline-summary tables, and a downstream-results table. These substantially expand the visual explanation and comparative evidence. Original plots are retained, with relocation, renumbering, and some caption revisions.

improvement.justification: The nonrandom baselines address an important weakness in v1's comparisons, while downstream classification and the method illustration add useful evidence and clarity. These gains are limited by unspecified experimental details and the unexplained relationship between retained SICK scores of 0.623–0.736 in Table 2 and 0.8426 in Figure 11. The abstract's new no-performance-loss claim also overstates the retained 77–95% transfer-effectiveness evidence. Overall, the additions improve the paper, but do not constitute fully reconciled, reproducible validation.
